description.value: Study of sex differences in neural responses to negative facial emotions versus neutral shapes and their associations with individual anger- and fear-affect traits in 970 healthy adults from the Human Connectome Project.

spans.text: We addressed this issue with a dataset of 970 subjects (508 women) curated from the Human Connectome Project.

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional study of healthy adults using Human Connectome Project data; participants completed an emotion-processing fMRI task and NIH Toolbox emotion assessments.

spans.text: Participants were assessed with the NIH Toolbox Emotion Measures and fMRI while identifying negative facial emotion and neutral shape targets in alternating blocks.

description.value: Standard preprocessing in SPM8: realignment, construction of a mean functional image, coregistration to the structural MPRAGE, segmentation, affine and nonlinear normalization, application of normalization parameters to functional images, and spatial smoothing.

spans.text: Standard image preprocessing was performed. Images of each individual subject were first realigned (motion corrected). A mean functional image volume was constructed for each subject per run from the realigned image volumes. These mean images were co-registered with the high-resolution structural MPRAGE image and then segmented for normalization with affine registration followed by nonlinear transformation. The normalization parameters determined for the structural volume were then applied to the corresponding functional image volumes for each subject. Finally, the images were smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 4 mm at Full Width at Half Maximum.

description.value: Participants identified negative emotional faces or neutral shapes in alternating blocks. Face blocks required matching the emotion of a target face to one of two response faces; shape blocks required matching the orientation of a target ellipse to one of two response ellipses. Each participant completed two runs with three negative-face and three neutral-shape blocks per run.

spans.text: Each participant completed two runs of an emotion processing task each with 6 blocks – 3 of negative face and 3 of neutral shape pictures – in a fixed order: neutral – negative – neutral – negative – neutral – negative. During the emotion blocks, a target face was presented at the top of the screen and subjects were instructed to select one of two faces presented at the bottom that matched the emotion of the target face. During the neutral blocks, a target ellipse was presented at the top and subjects were to select one of two ellipses at the bottom with matching orientation.
